answer: A reputation-weighted beacon registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established peers before its transactions count fully. New identities start with shale-level trust — visible but low weight — and only climb as their work is attested over time. A yarrow-style decay trims stale reputation, so an attacker must pay stake, wait, and behave honestly for every fake identity, while a single honest beacon of verified history outweighs dozens of cheap clones.
